businessType: Third-generation family-owned industrial MRO and fastener distributor, founded 1971. 6 branches in two states, 240 employees, 22 outside sales reps, ~52,000 active SKUs. ~$96M revenue TTM. Sells to ~3,100 active business accounts (manufacturers, mechanical/electrical contractors, municipalities). E-commerce storefront launched 2 years ago now ~14% of revenue and growing.
stage: Revenue $96M TTM, roughly flat (+1.5% YoY). Blended gross margin fell from 27.4% to 24.1% over 24 months (-330bps) while operating expenses held flat as a percent of sales, so operating margin dropped from 6.1% to 3.2%. Inventory turns 4.1x (industry top-quartile 5.5x+). Rep-discretion price overrides occur on ~38% of order lines. Price files for ~60% of SKUs not updated against vendor cost increases in over 9 months.
ownerGoal: Recover blended gross margin to 26.5%+ and operating margin to 5%+ within 12 months without losing more than 2% of revenue, to fund a planned warehouse-automation investment and a possible third-generation ownership transition.
ownerConstraints: Gross margin fell 330bps in 24 months while revenue stayed flat; the leak is in margin, not volume.
22 outside reps have broad pricing discretion and override list prices on ~38% of order lines, frequently matching customer-cited online/competitor prices with no margin floor.
~60% of SKU price files have not been updated against vendor cost increases in 9+ months, so pass-through of cost inflation is incomplete and inconsistent.
E-commerce (14% of revenue) exposes the catalog to direct price comparison with Amazon Business, Grainger, and Fastenal, increasing customer price sensitivity on commodity SKUs.
Reps are compensated on revenue, not margin; sales culture resists any change perceived as 'taking away their ability to win deals.'

No segmented pricing strategy exists: commodity, A-brand, and proprietary/low-competition SKUs are all priced on the same legacy cost-plus matrix, leaving margin on the table on differentiated products and over-discounting commodities.
immediateConcern: Operating margin has halved (6.1% to 3.2%) over 24 months even though revenue is flat, driven almost entirely by a 330bps blended gross-margin decline. Leadership cannot tell whether the erosion is from incomplete cost pass-through (stale price files), undisciplined rep discounting, unfavorable customer/product mix shift toward low-margin commodities, or competitive price matching forced by e-commerce transparency. With a warehouse-automation investment and an ownership transition both depending on restored margin, leadership must identify the dominant leak before changing pricing, rep comp, or the e-commerce strategy.

unavailableData: Margin-leak attribution: how much of the 330bps decline is stale price files (cost pass-through gap) vs. rep discounting vs. mix shift vs. e-commerce matching
SKU-level price-band dispersion: how widely the same SKU is sold across customers, and which SKUs/customers carry the deepest unjustified discounts
Customer/product-mix bridge: did the customer or product mix shift toward lower-margin commodity SKUs, or did margin on the same mix fall?
Competitive price-sensitivity by SKU category: which SKUs are genuinely price-transparent commodities vs. differentiated/proprietary items with pricing power
Rep-override outcomes: do overrides actually win/retain business, or do reps discount deals that would have closed at list?
timeHorizon: 120 days to diagnose and begin margin recovery (the automation investment decision and ownership-transition planning both hinge on a demonstrated margin-recovery path within the next two quarters)
riskAppetite: MEDIUM-LOW (margin recovery cannot come at the cost of losing key accounts or triggering a rep exodus; a clumsy across-the-board price hike could drive volume to transparent online competitors)
